purpose: Authoritative-provider delta adding MRPeasy manufacturing ERP/MRP after its August 2026 REST API v2 expansion. The connector reuses the REST/OpenAPI fabric, remains read-only, and introduces resource-scoped API-version routing because vendor documentation explicitly recommends v2 where available and v1 for functionality not yet present in v2. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, payroll mutation, private-network access or paid services were used.

systems.name: MRPeasy
systems.evidenceNote: Provider-owned MRPeasy documentation confirms HTTPS REST/OpenAPI APIs, Basic HTTP authentication using API key and secret, v1 plus an expanding v2 API, provider-recommended per-resource fallback from v2 to v1, v1 Range/206 pagination, v2 limit/offset pagination, HTTP 429 throttling, multi-site identifiers, custom manufacturing-order fields, manufacturing orders/production reports/workstations/routings, inventory, vendors, user action logs and v2 accounting/general-ledger data. August 2026 release notes confirm substantial new v2 endpoints for reports, dashboard data, production resources and stock. Exact API-key authority granularity, tenant/account identity, practical rate limits and complete endpoint parity require an authorised account.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Public documentation establishes an account API key/secret but does not prove a separately scoped read-only API credential. Before authentication evidence advances, prove the effective authority of a dedicated integration credential and denied POST/PUT/DELETE paths.

The same API surface exposes production and commercial mutations, including manufacturing-order create/update and customer-order actions that can trigger stock bookings/shipments. WFM must use an explicit GET/read route allowlist and never infer safety from successful Basic authentication.
MRPeasy v2 is explicitly incomplete and evolving. Version fallback must be resource-specific and provider-declared; 401/403/429/5xx responses must not trigger silent downgrade to v1.

requiredPermissions: use a dedicated API key/secret and keep it executor-boundary-only; never use a human password or persist Authorization headers in evidence/logs
pin HTTPS host api.mrpeasy.com and exact /rest/v1 or /rest/v2 read routes; disable cross-host redirects and arbitrary endpoints
allow only reviewed GET/read endpoints required for production, inventory, procurement, finance and audit context; keep POST/PUT/DELETE disabled
prove API key regeneration/deletion revocation and effective denied writes in an authorised account before tenant-authenticated evidence
negotiate API version per resource: prefer provider-documented v2 and use v1 only where the provider documents v2 absence/transition
namespace checkpoints by API version and pagination contract; replay/reconcile when switching between v1 Range pagination and v2 offset pagination
dataAvailableOrExpected: manufacturing orders with database IDs, product/article/BOM/routing references, assigned user, site, status, planned and real duration, due/start/finish dates and order cost fields
production order/operation/product reports for bounded date windows, supporting backlog and production-plan enrichment
workstations/workstation groups and routings/operations, including production-resource structure and cost/capacity context where exposed by the selected API version
inventory by site with on-hand quantity and cost, historical inventory snapshots, stock items/lots/serials, product groups, units of measurement and parameters
BOM/product references plus procurement/vendor data; vendor reads include lead time, on-time rate, average delay, spend and rejected-item metrics
customer orders and sales/shipping context where explicitly authorised, but commercial write actions remain disabled
v2 accounting/general-ledger transactions including manufacturing materials, routing/workstation overhead, labour-cost and finished-production actions
read-only user action logs with user/object/activity identifiers and creation timestamps for audit/provenance enrichment
customer-defined manufacturing-order custom fields using custom_<id> identifiers; preserve as source extensions until mapped
stableIdentifiers: preserve MRPeasy database IDs such as manufacturing-order, article/product, BOM, routing, workstation, site, vendor and transaction IDs as source identifiers
business codes such as manufacturing-order code, product code and vendor code may be useful matching keys but must not replace source database IDs
namespace every external key by customer MRPeasy account/connection and site where applicable; do not assume codes are globally unique across separate accounts

freshnessLatency.rest: polling-based; cadence is WFM-configured and constrained by MRPeasy throttling/response size. Preserve source dates/times separately from ingestion/recovery time.
freshnessLatency.reports: date-window reports are suitable for scheduled reconciliation/backfill rather than realtime event authority; some v1 production reports limit requested periods to one month.
freshnessLatency.webhooks: no provider webhook contract is relied on by this connector; scheduled reads and reconciliation remain the completeness mechanism.

paginationDeltaEvents.v1: many list endpoints use the Range request header and return 206 Partial Content for paged responses; checkpoints must retain the version and range boundary.
paginationDeltaEvents.v2: documented list endpoints use limit/offset, commonly with endpoint bounds up to 1000; 413 means the requested payload/page must be reduced.
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: there is no universal documented change-token contract across all objects. Use object-specific timestamps/filters where documented, bounded date windows for reports, overlapping reads and stable-ID dedupe/reconciliation rather than inventing CDC semantics.
paginationDeltaEvents.versionTransition: vendor explicitly recommends v2 where available and v1 otherwise. Fallback is capability-specific, never triggered by auth failure, rate limiting or transient server errors.

rateLimitsAndRetries: v1 endpoint documentation can return 429 when another request is running; v2 endpoints also document 429 Too Many Requests, so concurrency must be adaptively bounded rather than assuming high parallelism
no universal numeric quota is hard-coded; respect Retry-After when present, otherwise bounded exponential backoff with jitter for idempotent reads
401 stops blind retry and enters credential diagnostics; 403/permission-equivalent responses do not cause API-version downgrade
413 reduces v2 page size without changing semantic checkpoint; 429 and 5xx retry the same version rather than silently falling back
large backfills partition by object/site/date window, checkpoint after complete pages and reconcile counts/IDs across overlap windows
versionsRegionsCustomFields: v2 is an early-stage expanding API and August 2026 release notes added reports, dashboard, workstations/workstation groups/routings, inventory, critical on-hand, product groups, UOM and parameter endpoints; v1 remains required for gaps
v1 and v2 differ in route shape, pagination and some date representations, so version is part of provenance and checkpoint identity
MRPeasy is cloud based and supports multiple production sites/stocks in relevant plans; preserve site_id and separate account/connection identity for multi-site or acquired-company deployments

provider public material lists many supported countries/currencies, but API data-residency location and cross-border-transfer controls are not publicly proven; WFM must not infer residency from customer country
preserve source currency, site timezone, locale, units of measurement and Unix/date semantics explicitly rather than applying implicit conversions
manufacturing-order custom fields use account-specific custom_<id> names; schema negotiation must preserve unknown fields as extensions and review type/meaning changes
automationOpportunities: combine manufacturing-order backlog, planned/real duration and workstation/routing demand with WFM availability and skills to forecast overtime or agency need before shortages become end-of-shift emergencies
join site inventory/critical-on-hand and BOM demand to workforce plans so scarce skilled labour is not allocated to jobs that cannot run because material is unavailable
use vendor lead-time, on-time and rejected-item metrics to distinguish supplier-driven schedule risk from labour-driven risk and avoid blaming staffing for material-quality delays

join MRPeasy manufacturing labour/overhead ledger evidence with authoritative WFM pay cost to reconcile labour-per-order/unit and explain costing variance without treating ERP labour entries as payroll truth
use production actual/planned durations and completed-order outcomes to identify lines/work centres where redeployment or staffing changes have measurable throughput impact
bootstrap product, work-centre, routing, site, inventory, supplier and finance dimensions from one cloud source for smaller manufacturers, reducing implementation mapping effort
use user action logs and source IDs to improve provenance and explain when operational master data/order state changed around a workforce recommendation
savingsHypotheses: small manufacturers on MRPeasy can reduce implementation effort because one API source can populate production, work-centre, inventory, procurement and finance context without enterprise middleware
reduce overtime/agency spend by combining production-order lateness and real-vs-planned duration with internal worker availability/skills before capacity gaps become urgent
reduce paid idle time by detecting material-blocked work orders before labour is assigned and redirecting capacity to executable work
improve costing accuracy by reconciling MRPeasy production labour/overhead transactions against authoritative WFM labour cost and actual production output
reduce schedule disruption by factoring supplier on-time/rejection performance into labour planning rather than optimizing workforce against an infeasible material plan
reduce integration maintenance during the v1-to-v2 transition by using resource-scoped version negotiation and version-specific reconciliation instead of customer-specific forks
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve MRPeasy account/connection + site + source object ID, API version, schema fingerprint, source/effective time and ingestion time on every record
preserve recommendation/action IDs and baseline/outcome windows when WFM changes staffing against manufacturing-order, inventory or supplier-risk signals

retain competing changes such as material receipt/shortage, order priority change, routing/workstation change, supplier delay, customer-order change and production completion so throughput movement is not falsely attributed to labour changes
dataGaps: no authorised MRPeasy tenant was available to prove API-key scope, tenant/account identity, real schemas, practical rate limits, multi-site behaviour or denied writes
v2 is not functionally complete; resource coverage must be discovered against the current OpenAPI and never assumed from v1
no universal modified-since/change-token contract is publicly established across all objects, so delta sync remains object-specific plus reconciliation
MRPeasy is not an authoritative HCM/payroll source; assigned user and user-action data provide operational identity context only unless separately reconciled to workforce master data
public documentation reviewed does not establish customer-selectable API data residency; regional storage/transfer claims require contract/tenant evidence

quality/inspection data is commercially documented in reporting/integration material, but exact API object coverage must be confirmed per current OpenAPI before canonical quality mappings are promoted
constraintsRisks: REST API is available only on the paid Unlimited plan, so smaller customers on lower tiers may require existing file/manual/iPaaS routes rather than API automation
API key/secret uses Basic authentication and effective resource/write scoping is not publicly demonstrated; treat it as potentially broad until tenant evidence proves otherwise
v1 and v2 coexist with different pagination and route semantics; generic fallback on any error would risk masking credential, rate-limit or outage problems
several endpoints expose mutations with real inventory/production/commercial effects, so method/route allowlisting is mandatory
custom fields and separate customer accounts can create schema and identifier collisions unless source connection/site/version remain part of provenance
rate limiting may make highly parallel backfills counterproductive; elastic scaling must respect provider concurrency rather than equating tenant size with connector concurrency
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain an authorised MRPeasy Unlimited test account. Prove account identity and dedicated API-key authority, denied POST/PUT/DELETE routes, key rotation/deletion revocation, current v1/v2 OpenAPI coverage, resource-scoped version negotiation, v1 Range versus v2 offset pagination, 413 page reduction, 429 backoff, multi-site identity, custom_<id> field drift, currency/UOM/time handling and overlap/backfill reconciliation. Keep production/customer-order mutations disabled.
